title: Collinearity analysis of multi-replicon bacterial genomes (Vibrio spp.)
summary: Two Vibrio genomes, each with two chromosomes. Each chromosome is rotated in gbdraw to start at its replication initiator gene — dnaA on chromosome I and rctB on chromosome II — so records that NCBI starts at unrelated positions line up. Inversions occur within each chromosome, but collinear blocks rarely connect chromosome I to chromosome II. This tutorial adds the two assemblies, generates with the defaults, runs LOSATP Collinear blocks once, rotates each chromosome to its initiator, and finishes the figure; every Generate after the first comparison reuses the LOSAT results.
primaryWorkflow: Align replicons at their replication origin

manualSteps.title: Generate with the defaults
manualSteps.body: Click Generate Diagram. Arrange in rows is on by default and puts each File's records in one row, so each species gets a row with chromosome I on the left and chromosome II on the right. With two records in a row, Auto hides Accession and Length / Coordinates and Replicon is off by default, so each row is labelled only with its species and strain. Nothing yet shows which regions the two genomes share.

manualSteps.title: Compare the genomes with LOSATP Collinear blocks
manualSteps.body: To see which regions the genomes share, compare their proteins. In Comparison, choose Run LOSAT. Open Settings, press LOSATP, set LOSATP mode, Color mode, Max unit gap, and Min block genes, and turn on Build similarity groups with within-record searches, as the command line does by default. Set Diagonal drift under Advanced comparison and layout, then click Generate Diagram. The ribbons run diagonally and wrap around the row ends, because NCBI starts each chromosome at an unrelated position.

rows: Build similarity groups with within-record searches

manualSteps.title: Start chromosome I at dnaA
manualSteps.body: Start each chromosome I at its replication initiator, dnaA. In the search bar above the preview, set the search field to Qualifier value, type gene as the Qualifier key and dnaA as the query, and click Search; it finds the dnaA CDS of both species. Click Open, then in the popup open Rotate record using this feature, choose Start of the record, and click Apply when I Generate. Click > for the second match; the open popup follows it. Rotate that record the same way, then close the popup.
manualSteps.note: Both initiators are on the + strand, so each record keeps its orientation. The new starts apply at the next Generate.

manualSteps.title: Finish the figure
manualSteps.body: At genome scale the arrowheads crowd into noise and the preview has no coordinates. In Features, draw all seven feature types as rectangles and set the stroke widths. In Layout, set Track Layout to Above; Separate Strands and Lock Definition Column are already on. In Axis & Scale, draw a ruler on each axis every 750,000 bp. In Titles & Record Labels, set the record-label fonts.

manualSteps.title: Generate and check the result
manualSteps.body: Click Generate Diagram. Generate again reuses the LOSAT results. Check the result:
items: Each row starts at its replication initiator, so the ruler counts from dnaA at the left end of chromosome I and from rctB at the left end of chromosome II.
Red (inverted) blocks join regions within chromosome I or within chromosome II.
Few blocks cross from chromosome I of one species to chromosome II of the other.

losatTips.title: Load the session to skip the LOSATP search
losatTips.body: The Gallery session holds the finished figure, every setting, and the LOSATP results. Load it to inspect the result at once.

losatTips.title: Expect a long first run
losatTips.body: LOSATP compares four chromosome pairs of about 1.7 to 3.3 Mbp. The Gallery figure was made on the command line with 16 threads. In the browser, Safe leaves CPU cores free for the rest of the page.

losatTips.title: Rotation and style changes reuse the LOSATP search
losatTips.body: After the first run, Generate reuses the LOSATP results for rotations, colors, and layout changes. Changing a chromosome, file, input order, or LOSAT threshold runs that pair's LOSATP search again.

troubleshooting.title: The search finds no feature
troubleshooting.body: Set the search field to Qualifier value and type the qualifier key: gene for dnaA, product for RctB.

troubleshooting.title: A record does not start at its initiator
troubleshooting.body: Apply when I Generate waits for the next Generate Diagram. Check Display start in each record's Record options in its File card.

troubleshooting.title: Accession or length appears under a species
troubleshooting.body: Open Titles & Record Labels and set Accession and Length / Coordinates back to Auto, or to Hide; leave Replicon off.

troubleshooting.title: The browser becomes unresponsive
troubleshooting.body: Load the bundled session, switch LOSAT execution to Serial, or lower the thread budget before the full LOSATP search.
